To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the degree of separation between operational responsibilities and governance is higher in private non-profit nursing homes compared to public non-profit nursing homes and that this separation is positively related to size.

(1) separation between operational responsibilities and the oversight function is an important point in governance; (2) this separation increases with organization size in private institutions but not in public institutions; and (3) this lack in flexibility explains micro-monitoring in the public sector.
(a) the separation between governance and operational responsibilities is higher in large nursing homes; and (b) this is not the same for private and public institutions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the separation between operational responsibilities and oversight responsibilities.
the governance of non-profit organizations.
the separation between operational and oversight responsibilities in non-profit nursing homes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in private homes, size is associated with more governance separation, which is beneficial for efficiency, while public institutions do not seem to benefit from this separation.
the governance structure of public non-profit organizations should be more flexible to allow for the optimal degree of separation of governance roles.
the degree of separation between governance and operational responsibilities increases with size, and this is especially true for privately owned nursing homes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the separation between governance and operations is an important aspect of the governance structure of non-profit nursing homes, but that it should be implemented in a flexible manner, depending on the size and ownership of the institution.
the governance practices of non-profit nursing homes are not only influenced by ownership characteristics, but also by their size.
the degree of separation is related to ownership characteristics and that this is related to size.
The main takeaway from our work is that
size and ownership characteristics of nursing homes are related to the degree of separation in governance.
the degree of separation in governance should be determined by the specific characteristics of the institution and not be a priori prescribed by the government.
the governance structure of non-profits can be improved by allowing for more flexibility in the separation of operational responsibilities and those related to the oversight.
